headline: Still no run in a week — the restart pair never became a habit. The Åre block keeps the base intact, but strength and a fresh threshold read stay untouched. Priority remains simply re-establishing contact.
confidence_reasons: No recent activity data in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture is one of a strong recent block sitting increasingly idle. Running has been dark for a full week now; the two short faster efforts that hinted at a restart never gained a third leg, and the big Åre stretch before them is now weeks in the rear-view. That said, the base itself is not in question — the four-week volume is still enormously up on the prior block, and the year-to-date distance dwarfs last year. Strength remains the quietest corner of all, with only sparse sessions in the last month and no recent anchor to speak of. Steps stay high and remarkably flat between training and rest days, so background movement is carrying real load even when nothing is logged. The absence of a valid cardio-load reading means there's no strain signal to lean on right now — the story is being told entirely by the gap in the run calendar.
sections.trends: The 16-week shape is a clear spike-then-silence: a large durability-heavy block peaking through Åre, followed by two short high-intensity touches, then nothing. Against the year-to-date monthly progression this is still a strong year by every volume measure, so the current quiet stretch reads as an inter-block trough rather than a decline. What it isn't yet is a rhythm — the training has swung between long trail volume and short speed touches without settling into a repeatable weekly cadence, which is the one thing the recent shape is missing relative to the athlete's year-round-readiness intent.
sections.threshold: The threshold figure is now two months old and is comfortably the stalest signal on the board. Nothing since has tested that range in a sustained way — the Åre work sat almost entirely in Z1 by design, and the two recent short runs touched the top end only in brief spikes. So the current threshold number should be read as a historical marker, not a live reading of where aerobic fitness sits today. Until a clean sustained tempo effort lands, any statement about current threshold fitness is inference from base rather than measurement.
sections.zones: The recent distribution is bimodal in the least useful way: enormous Z1 volume from the trail block at one end, and two runs with genuine Z3–Z4 minutes at the other, with the sustained-threshold middle almost entirely absent. The two August runs are the only sessions carrying real time above easy, and even those were mixed-effort rather than steady — useful for reintroducing top-end range but not for filling the grey-zone gap. For a hybrid block trying to hold both ends, the polarisation is defensible; the missing piece is a controlled tempo that occupies the middle deliberately rather than by accident.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength HR remains sparse and sits where you'd expect for functional work — mostly low aerobic with occasional pushes into the middle zones, nothing that reads as a maximal grind. There's no meaningful Garmin-vs-Polar disagreement to flag; the recent runs that carried a chest strap tracked cleanly through their range. Nothing here changes the read.
sections.calendar: The calendar tells the real story this week: a dense, high-volume cluster through mid-August, then a hard stop. Both running and strength streaks have reset to zero, and the gap has now stretched from "a few cold days" to a genuine week without contact. This isn't a taper — there's no event to taper for — so the most honest read is an unplanned pause rather than a structured deload. The base earned in August buys tolerance for that, but the longer the silence runs the more it becomes the defining feature rather than a footnote.
sections.personal_bests: The short-distance PBs from last autumn remain well clear of anything the current block has demonstrated — the recent fast touches showed top-end range but over very short distances at mixed effort. Nothing in the present data suggests a PB is imminent; the fitness that set those marks would need a rebuilt speed-endurance base first. Not a relevant target this week.

watch_items: Watch whether any run lands at all — the priority is still re-establishing contact, and a full week now makes that the single most important thing to observe.
Watch whether strength reappears in any form, since it has no recent anchor and both streaks have reset.
Watch whether a clean sustained tempo finally shows up — it's the one session that would refresh the stale threshold and fill the missing middle.
Watch whether the next block commits to a lane rather than continuing to alternate between long trail volume and short speed touches.
